## Hackster launches Emotion in Motion robotics design challenge with Renesas and Arduino


November 17, 2026


*Developers invited to explore emotion, voice and movement using the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi powered by the Renesas RA4M1 microcontroller*


PHOENIX – Hackster, an Avnet community, has launched Emotion in Motion, a robotics design challenge inviting developers, engineers, makers and students to create projects exploring emotion, voice and motor control. Hackster is giving away 500 Arduino® UNO R4 WiFi boards, powered by the Renesas RA4M1 microcontroller, to help participants bring their ideas to life.


Emotion in Motion challenges participants to explore the more human side of robotics and electronics. Projects can mimic or respond to emotions, interact through voice, demonstrate fine motor skills and dexterity, play and react, or help people complete tasks.


“Robotics isn't only about what a machine can do, but increasingly how naturally people can interact with it,” said Dianne Kibbey, Senior Director, Community Strategy and Hackster.io at Avnet. “Emotion in Motion challenges our community to explore that intersection, using hardware to rethink how electronics can respond, move and interact with the people around them.”


Participants can submit projects across five categories, ranging from emotionally intelligent robots and voice-enabled experiences to machines demonstrating articulation, dexterity and fine motor control.


The seven top qualifying projects will receive prizes totaling $14,500, including a $5,000 first-place prize.


To learn more about the Emotion in Motion design challenge, visit the[Hackster challenge page](https://www.hackster.io/contests/emotion-in-motion) .
